title: NP recognition of closed hyperbolic three-manifolds
formal: Does there exist a deterministic polynomial-time verifier V and a polynomial p such that, for every finite PL-triangulation T of a compact connected three-manifold M, M is closed and admits a hyperbolic metric if and only if there exists a binary certificate w with |\(w|\le p(|T|)\) and \(V(T,w)=1\)?
why: Would show that a global constant-curvature geometry can always be certified using polynomially bounded discrete evidence from an arbitrary triangulation. It would sharpen the complexity of a central geometric recognition problem beyond mere decidability.
status_note: Original manifold and triangulation conventions recovered, and subsequent-work searches checked through 11 September 2026; no matching NP-resolution result located. Related cusped non-hyperbolicity results have different promises and answer direction. Proofs were not independently audited.

progress.text: The 2024 report attributes decidability of hyperbolic recognition to Casson and Manning, while retaining the stronger NP question.

Haraway and Hoffman give non-hyperbolicity certificates in the cusped orientable setting; their Theorem 1 assumes \(S^{3}\) recognition lies in coNP, while their irreducible cusped case is unconditional.
Schleimer explicitly poses NP recognition of closed hyperbolic three-manifolds as Question 12.

sentences: The input describes a compact connected three-manifold by gluing faces of finitely many tetrahedra.
The question is whether being closed and admitting a hyperbolic metric always has a polynomial-size certificate.
A single deterministic verifier must check such certificates in polynomial time for every input triangulation.
Recognition is decidable, but this does not give the required certificate-size and verification-time bounds.
A positive answer would connect a global geometric structure with short, efficiently verifiable combinatorial evidence.

upgraded_from.title: NP recognition of closed hyperbolic three-manifolds

definitions: The input consists of t abstract tetrahedra and a finite list of affine face identifications, each encoded by two tetrahedron indices, face indices and a permutation of the face vertices. Unpaired faces are permitted. Identifying these faces produces the quotient space \(M=|T|\). The input is promised to be a PL-triangulation of a compact connected topological three-manifold, possibly with boundary; no orientability or irreducibility promise is imposed. Its encoding length |T| counts all bits in the explicit tetrahedron and face-pairing data, with binary indices. Closed means that M has empty boundary, since compactness is already promised. A hyperbolic metric means a Riemannian metric locally isometric to hyperbolic three-space \(H^{3}\); for example \(H^{3}\) is the upper half-space \(\{(x,y,z)\in \mathbb{R} ^{3}:z>0\}\) with metric \(ds^{2}=(dx^{2}+dy^{2}+dz^{2})/z^{2}\). Equivalently, the metric has constant sectional curvature −1. On closed M it is complete. The abstract tetrahedra in the input are topological data and are not supplied as geometric tetrahedra in that metric. V is one uniform deterministic Turing algorithm without advice or an oracle, and runs in time polynomial in |T|+|w| on all encoded inputs. Correctness is required on every promised manifold triangulation; no particular certificate format or method is prescribed. The polynomial certificate bound and verifier are fixed for the entire problem, not chosen separately for each manifold.
answer_criterion: Give a polynomial certificate bound and a uniform polynomial-time verifier that accepts some bounded-length certificate for every closed hyperbolic input and accepts none for every other promised manifold input. Alternatively, prove that no such bound and verifier exist. A terminating recognition algorithm alone, or certificates for non-hyperbolicity, do not establish this NP membership.

context_blocks.title: Geometry from a finite gluing description
context_blocks.text: The input says which faces of finitely many tetrahedra are glued together. It determines a topological space, but does not hand the verifier a hyperbolic metric. The question asks whether existence of that global geometric structure always has a short, efficiently checkable witness.

context_blocks.title: The certificate must work for every triangulation
context_blocks.text: Two very different gluing descriptions can represent the same manifold. A successful verifier must accept every description of a closed hyperbolic manifold with some certificate polynomial in that description’s size. It cannot be limited to triangulations that visibly carry a convenient geometric structure.

context_blocks.title: Decidable versus efficiently certifiable
context_blocks.text: Schleimer’s 2024 report records decidability of hyperbolic recognition and separately asks for NP membership. Decidability guarantees eventual termination; NP requires a polynomial bound on both the witness size and verification work.

context_blocks.title: Boundary and answer direction both matter
context_blocks.text: Haraway and Hoffman study non-hyperbolicity certificates for orientable manifolds with torus boundary. Their results give coNP statements about hyperbolicity in that setting. The present question concerns positive certificates for closed hyperbolic manifolds, so it has both a different input class and a different answer direction.
